dedupe_keys.name: national coastal erosion indicator for france cerema 2026 update and geolittoral shoreline data

description: The national coastal erosion indicator, produced by Cerema with the support of the French ministry for ecological transition, describes past shoreline change along the coasts of mainland France, Corsica and the overseas departments and regions. It is based on old and recent aerial photographs; the 2026 update uses more shorelines over several years, includes harmonised data from the regional shoreline observatories, and computes results on about 126,000 profiles every 50 metres along the coast. Results for the 1950s to 2020 show about 20 percent of natural coasts retreating and 27.6 percent of the whole seafront affected by erosion, rising to 50.1 percent of beaches, and nearly one beach profile in two shows a reversal of trend. Results are available online in a Cerema map application (a web viewer) and explained in a study report, and the Géolittoral shoreline data page also lists historical shorelines and the Ortho littorale aerial photo campaigns. Content is free under the Etalab 2.0 licence unless stated otherwise. Caveats: the page says the indicator describes past change and does not explain local causes, and it should be complemented by local studies. It supports coastal flood and erosion exposure analysis of coastal roads, ports, networks and defences; the related record is the Coastal Flood Exposure Mapper of NOAA.
